changelog.note: Initial 10 questions from the SRO 1468 DISCO adjustment table. Baseline hit@1 0.00, hit@3 0.125, hit@5 0.25, hit@10 0.50.
Corrected source_page from printed page labels to PDF page indices. SRO 1468 opens with an unnumbered cover page. Scores rose to hit@1 0.00, hit@3 0.25, hit@5 0.75, hit@10 1.00.

Introduced acceptable_sources. TRF-100 (the Authority's determination) and SRO 1468 (the gazette notification of that same determination) contain the SAME DISCO adjustment table. v2 scored only SRO 1468 as correct, so a retriever returning the identical table from TRF-100 was marked wrong. That measured document preference, not retrieval quality, and it was the systematic cause of hit@1 = 0/8. A question is now a hit if ANY acceptable source is retrieved. Schema bumped to 2.0: source_doc/source_page are replaced by acceptable_sources.

page_number_convention: page is the PDF PAGE INDEX, 1-based, counting every physical page including unnumbered covers. NOT the label printed in the footer.
_readme: GROUND TRUTH. Verified against source PDFs only.
acceptable_sources — every {doc, page} where the answer genuinely appears.
A retrieval is a hit if ANY of them is returned. Regulatory corpora are
full of duplication: determinations, notifications, and SROs restate the
same tables. Insisting on one canonical location measures the wrong thing.
The FIRST entry is the primary source, used when reporting which document
a citation should prefer. The rest are equally correct for scoring.
1. Nothing enters this file unverified against the PDF.
2. Retrieval and answer accuracy are scored separately.
3. Expected failures are the valuable questions. Keep them.
4. FROZEN means frozen. Errors become v4 with a changelog entry.
Document matching is by token overlap at 0.6. Once 40 near-identical
quarterly decisions are indexed this will match the wrong quarter
('4th' vs '3rd' is the only differing token). Replace with explicit
doc_id matching BEFORE expanding the corpus.

failure_mode_taxonomy.column_mapping: OCR corrupts table headers, so a value cannot be reliably matched to its column.
failure_mode_taxonomy.sign_handling: Accounting parentheses denote negatives. Read as positive, the answer inverts.
failure_mode_taxonomy.number_corruption: OCR alters digits or separators: (3.319) for (3,319).
failure_mode_taxonomy.unit_in_header: The unit sits in a header row far from the figure; chunking separates them.
failure_mode_taxonomy.split_row_label: A row label wraps across two lines and chunking severs it from its values.
failure_mode_taxonomy.small_text_extraction: Low-contrast or small print extracts unreliably.
failure_mode_taxonomy.aggregation: Requires summing or cross-checking several values.
failure_mode_taxonomy.temporal_disambiguation: Several dates or periods appear close together; the right one must be selected.
failure_mode_taxonomy.cross_document: The answer lives in a different document than the one most similar to the question.
failure_mode_taxonomy.duplicate_source: The answer appears in more than one document. Tests whether scoring credits any valid location.
failure_mode_taxonomy.refusal: The corpus does not contain the answer. The only correct behaviour is to say so.

questions.question: What was the total quarterly adjustment for MEPCO in the 4th quarter of FY 2024-25?
questions.notes: Header row is OCR-corrupted. The 6th value in the row must be mapped to MEPCO without a reliable header.

questions.question: Did QESCO's total quarterly adjustment increase or decrease in Q4 FY 2024-25?
questions.answer: Increased. QESCO is the only DISCO with a positive value: +3,594 million rupees. All others are negative.
questions.notes: Failed in v2 because top-1 was TRF-100. If TRF-100 carries the same table, this was never a retrieval failure.

questions.question: What was PESCO's capacity charges figure for Q4 FY 2024-25?
questions.notes: Extraction reads (3.319) with a decimal point. Correct value is 3,319 — a system trusting the extraction is wrong by 1000x.

questions.question: What was the total negative quarterly adjustment allowed across all XWDISCOs for Q4 FY 2024-25?
questions.notes: Verified: the ten DISCO values sum exactly to this total. Automatable as a validation rule later.

questions.question: What was the circular debt payable to power producers for FY 2023-24, and for FY 2024-25?
questions.answer: FY 2023-24 (Jul 23 to Jun 24): 1,600 billion rupees. FY 2024-25 (Jul 24 to Jun 25): 861 billion rupees.
questions.notes: Small, low-contrast print. Both values must be returned correctly paired to their fiscal years, not merely found.

questions.question: On what date did the Authority decide the Federal Government's Motion for a uniform consumer-end tariff?

acceptable_sources._todo: FILL — the same opening paragraph likely appears in both

questions.notes: Three dates within two sentences: June 14 2024 (determination), July 11 2024 (Motion decided), July 1 2024 (effective). Retrieval finds the paragraph; the test is whether the right date is picked from it.

questions.question: What market operation fee per kW per month did the Authority ALLOW CPPA-G for FY 2024-25, including legal charges?
questions.answer: REFUSAL — the corpus holds the covering document, not the full determination containing the allowed figure.
questions.notes: Became a refusal question once the 7-page TRF-615 file turned out to be the covering letter rather than the 33-page determination. If you later add the full determination, this returns to a cross_document question.

questions.question: What was the quarterly tariff adjustment for FESCO in the 1st quarter of FY 2025-26?
questions.answer: REFUSAL — the corpus does not contain this information.
questions.notes: A near-miss by design. FESCO is in the corpus, quarterly adjustments are in the corpus, the phrasing matches answerable questions exactly — only the period is absent. Retrieval will confidently return the Q4 FY2024-25 table. A system that invents a figure here is the one that loses a client.
